text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
DAWN
- Malaysia led the list of 12 countries with which Pakistan ran a huge trade deficit in fiscal 1995/96 (July-June).
- A government committee said big farmers were hoarding cotton, making it difficult to estimate the actual crop size.
- President Farooq Leghari's counsel Khalid Anwar told the Supreme Court that the government was a partner of the Sindh government in the extra-judicial killings in Karachi.
- Former cricketer-turned-politician Imran Khan asked President Farooq Leghari to step down immediately for colluding with plunderers of the national wealth.
BUSINESS RECORDER
- The government has amended the law to allow scripless trading in shares, thereby permitting the Central Depository Company to become operational within two months.
- Due diligence being conducted for the listing of a $150 million Exchangeable Bond issue of Pakistan Telecommunication Company Ltd is reportedly in a fairly advanced stage.
- The government has transferred partial working interests of Premier Exploration Pakistan Ltd in five oil and gas exploration blocks to Novus Pakistan Ltd.
- Iran has shown keen interest in purchasing Pakistani rice.
FINANCIAL POST
- The government is considering de-regulation and privatisation of petroleum imports and freight.
THE NATION
- The caretaker government has conceded to two more conditions of the International Monetary Fund for securing release of second $76 million tranche of the standby loan.
THE MUSLIM

- Most political parties have rejected the agreement signed between the federal government and the four provincial governments for the distribution of resources, saying an unelected government had no right to sign such a document.
- Senate Chairman Wasim Sajjad scuttled a debate in the upper house on the formation of Council for Defence and National Security by proroguing the house sine die.
THE NEWS
- State (Central) Bank Governor Muhammad Yaqub asked investment banks to separate their ownership from management.
--Islamabad newsroom 9251-274757
